title: Model Release Adapter: Constraint-Sensitive Orchestration and Shadow Isolation
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Problem: We need a composable 'Model Release Adapter' that compiles a single model release intent into environment-specific deployment actions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. Current orchestration assumes broad parity and fails when environment constraints (eg. VPC egress rules, HSM-backed KMS, limited burst capacity on Dedicated pools, and air-gapped Private sites) require different canary/shadow strategies or stricter safety budgets.

Goal: Implement a translator that takes a canonical rollout plan (traffic split, canary duration, metric guards, synthetic traffic profile) and emits per-environment plans that respect constraints and recommend mitigation actions. The adapter should: 1) detect environment capability gaps, 2) synthesize safe shadowing strategies when direct mirroring would violate policies, 3) recommend adjusted canary sizes and timings for Dedicated/Private, and 4) produce machine-executable deployment patches for the orchestration layer.

Why now: Increased enterprise adoption of Dedicated/Private means more rollouts failing late due to 'surprise' constraints. We must reduce manual intervention, shorten release cycles, and avoid risky ad-hoc rollbacks for high-SLA customers.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical rollout manifest can be translated into per-environment execution plans with documented diffs for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
Adapter flags environment capability mismatches (eg. missing egress, KMS differences, lack of burst capacity) and emits mitigation recommendations.
Shadow traffic for Private sites can be implemented without egress by running local replay-only instances or synthetic ingress generation; adapter emits required stub configs.
Automated canary sizing rules reduce default canary from 5% to environment-appropriate min (eg. 1% for Private with limited tenant isolation) and record rationale in plan.
Auto-rollback triggers are configurable per-environment and include hysteresis to avoid flapping; integration tests simulate rollback on metric breach.

End-to-end integration test validates a multi-mode rollout that runs Hosted canary + Dedicated partial shadow + Private replay, with expected observability markers and no unsafe network calls to customer VPCs.
Design doc reviewed and approved by Infra and Security; implementation merged and a demo run is executed with SRE present.
comments: 2025-11-12 - Aisha Moreno: Initial ticket created after two incidents where Private rollouts were blocked by egress/VPC rules. Collected examples from support and SRE playbooks.

2025-11-14 - Jared Liu: Spike completed to enumerate environment capability matrix. Found three core mismatches: network egress constraints, KMS/HSM availability, and dedicated pool burst limits. See spike notes in Confluence.

2025-11-15 - Design review (Infra + Security): Agreed on a translator + templates approach vs full-blown DSL to keep scope small. Security requested formal approval flow for any config that touches customer KMS/HSM.

2025-11-16 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1987 - prototype translator and sample templates for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Feedback requested from runtime team on KV cache compatibility flags.

2025-11-17 - Runtime feedback (Noah Patel): Suggest exposing 'cache-compat' and 'kernel-profile' labels from model metadata so adapter can pick safe model variant when Private environment lacks quantized kernels. Added TODO to PR.

2025-11-18 - SRE note (Melanie Cruz): We'll run a controlled demo next week with synthetic traffic generator 'rollout-replay' to validate shadow isolation. Also flagged alert thresholds to be lowered for the demo to test rollback plumbing.

2025-11-18 - Action items: 1) Add environment capability detector as library (Jared), 2) Add approval UI stub to Console for KMS/HSM touching changes (Design/Console), 3) Write integration test harness that runs triple-mode rollout simulation (SRE + QE).
notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) fidelity vs maintainability — we avoid full DSL to limit surface area and rely on template patches plus a capability matrix. 2) conservative defaults vs developer speed — default to stricter canary sizes in Private unless an explicit exception is approved.

Open questions: How to represent hardware kernel mismatches in the capability matrix? Proposal: three-level label per model (full, partial, degraded) with recommended alternate model variants for degraded hosts.
Risk: If adapter recommends model fallback (eg. quantized variant) we must ensure quality regressions are surfaced to the release owner via Eval hooks before rollout continues.
Operational considerations: Need a Console affordance that shows the per-environment diffs and a one-click approval for security-reviewed changes (esp. KMS/HSM).
